title: Altitude sets the order
standfirst: Most Peru itineraries get the order wrong and the first three days are spent recovering.

blocks.heading: Valley before Cusco, always
paras: Cusco sits higher than the Sacred Valley, and arriving straight into it from sea level is the reason so many people lose a day.
We send members to the valley first, give it two nights, and bring them up to the city afterwards.

blocks.heading: The sites, privately
blocks.caption: Private access hours at the major sites.
paras: The headline sites now run timed entry and are busiest in the middle of the day.
Early and late slots are bookable in advance and change the experience completely.

blocks.heading: The Amazon as its own week
blocks.caption: The rainforest runs on a different calendar.
paras: The jungle is not an add-on to the highlands. It has its own season, its own pace and its own travel time.
We treat it as a separate week or leave it for another trip rather than bolting on three nights.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: May to September is dry in the highlands. The Amazon runs differently and is good for much of the year.
Manageable if the order is right. We build in the valley first and keep the first day deliberately empty.
Both work. The expedition trains are genuinely good and suit members who would rather spend the days elsewhere.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
